Synopsis:
Heading into the Sept 15-16 Fed meeting, markets are laser-focused on the Aug 11 CPI print as the decisive data point for whether the Fed hikes or holds. Fed Governor Waller signaled a preference to hold if inflation continues cooling, pushing hike odds to roughly 50/50. The S&P 500 sits near record highs (+13% YTD), but September seasonality, elevated yields (10Y at 4.77%), AI trade rotation, and geopolitical risk are cited as headwinds. Goldman Sachs base case is a hold, with a hike conditional on upside CPI/PPI surprises.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (YES — the article is centrally about the Fed rate decision trajectory, CPI inflation data, and their direct impact on Treasury yields and equity markets)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 70 (actively debated as a live scenario for the Sept meeting)
Probability of increase: ~50% (Fed funds futures at time of writing implied roughly even odds of a hike)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 70 (Waller's comments and Goldman's base case both lean toward a hold)
Probability of holding: ~50% (mirror of hike odds; Goldman base case but explicitly conditional on CPI/PPI)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (cuts are not mentioned or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -20 (Mildly dovish tilt — the most recent data point is Waller's Thursday comments favoring a hold if inflation cools, pulling hike odds back from elevated levels; however, a hike remains squarely on the table, preventing a fully dovish read)
